precepts.text: Elias is come already, and they knew him not; the disciples understood that he spake unto them of John the Baptist.
precepts.point: The son of Zacharias was John the Baptist, a Levite; and John the Baptist was Elijah back on the earth again, come to do what was prophesied of him. There is no reincarnation, coming back as a bird or such; there is regeneration, and we come back over and over again.

note.label: Numbers 4: The Service of the Tabernacle Done in Order

precepts.why:
The son of Zacharias was John the Baptist, a Levite of that priestly line. And John the Baptist was Elijah back on the earth again, come to do what was prophesied of him. “But I say unto you, That Elias is come already, and they knew him not, but have done unto him whatsoever they listed. Likewise shall also the Son of man suffer of them. Then the disciples understood that he spake unto them of John the Baptist.”

There is no reincarnation, coming back as a bird or such; there is regeneration, and we come back over and over again. Elias came already as John the Baptist, and they knew him not.

precepts.text: Moses and Elias appeared talking with Christ on the mount; Moses is good.
precepts.point: Moses is still good; he stood with Elias before Christ on the mount. He missed the promised land at that time, not the kingdom. But leadership carries the greater condemnation: the more given unto you, the more stripes when you fail.

note.label: Deuteronomy 1: The Second Giving of the Law

precepts.why:
“And, behold, there appeared unto them Moses and Elias talking with him.” Moses is still good. The judgment at the waters kept him out of the promised land at that time, but it did not keep him out of the kingdom: he stood with Elias before Christ on the mount, talking with him.

So “Thou also shalt not go in thither” was the loss of the land, not of the kingdom. But it stands as the warning for leadership, which carries the greater condemnation: the more given unto you, the more stripes when you fail, and Moses, who was given so much, missed the land for one failure at the rock.

precepts.text: A voice out of the cloud says, "This is my beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased; hear ye him," showing Christ is the only other prophet the Most High dealt with face to face and put his words in his mouth.
precepts.point: "Like unto thee," like unto Moses, means the same similarities: Moses spoke to the Most High directly, mediated between the Most High and Israel, gave the laws, was hidden as a child when the young were sought to be killed, and led Israel toward the promised land.

note.label: Acts 3: The Restitution of All Things

precepts.why:
“While he yet spake, behold, a bright cloud overshadowed them: and behold a voice out of the cloud, which said, This is my beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased; hear ye him.”

Hear ye him: the same words Moses used, him shall ye hear in all things. Christ is the only other prophet the Most High dealt with face to face and put his words in his mouth.

Like unto Moses means the same similarities. Moses spoke to the Most High directly, mediated between the Most High and Israel, gave the laws, was hidden as a child when the young were sought to be killed, and led Israel toward the promised land. Christ is that prophet.

precepts.text: Moses and Elias appear, but the voice out of the cloud says this is my beloved Son, hear ye him, showing the name and authority is Christ's, not another man's.
precepts.point: You cannot sneak into the kingdom through Islam, the Nation of Islam, Jehovah's Witnesses, Mormonism, Pentecostalism, Seventh-day Adventism, the Baptists, or Buddhism. Whoever climbs up some other way is a thief and a robber trying to sneak in without laboring; you must enter by the door, which is Christ.

note.label: Acts 4: The Stone the Builders Rejected

precepts.why:
On the mount “there appeared unto them Moses and Elias talking with him”, and Peter wanted to build three tabernacles, “one for thee, and one for Moses, and one for Elias.” But the voice out of the cloud singled out one: “This is my beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased; hear ye him.”

None other name means no other power or authority was given to any man. Christians reduce it to saying the words in the name of Jesus, but the name is the authority, and that authority was given to Christ alone. There is no salvation in Moses or Elias, only through Christ.

note.label: WHEN CHILDREN WALK IN A LAND OF SHADOWS

precepts.why: “And Jesus answered and said unto them, Elias truly shall first come, and restore all things.” Elias is the Greek way of saying Elijah. Christ is making reference to Malachi chapter 4: Elijah shall truly come, and restore all things. Turning the hearts of the fathers and the children is that restoring.

note.label: Flawed Apologetic Doctrine

precepts.why: The Father bears record in heaven: “behold a voice out of the cloud, which said, This is my beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased; hear ye him.” If Christ were the Father, it would say, this is me, in whom I am well pleased, hear me. The Lord is not the author of confusion.

note.label: Assata & Saddam: a Tale of 2 Revolutions

precepts.why:
This is what “Then are the children free” means. “The sons also of them that afflicted thee shall come bending unto thee; and all they that despised thee shall bow themselves down at the soles of thy feet”: everybody that hates us is going to bow down at the soles of our feet. “And they shall call thee, The city of the Lord, The Zion of the Holy One of Israel”: that’s what we’re going to be called.

“Whereas thou hast been forsaken and hated”: we were forsaken of all nations, hated of all nations. “So that no man went through thee”: no man took care of us, no nation looked after us. “I will make thee an eternal excellency, a joy of many generations”: God is going to make us, the Israelites, an eternal excellency and a joy of many generations.

“Thou shalt also suck the milk of the Gentiles, and shalt suck the breast of kings”: the milk of the Gentiles means their wealth. Everything’s going to come back to us. “For brass I will bring gold, and for iron I will bring silver”: this is the wealth he’s going to give us.

“I will also make thy officers peace”: y’all think officers is something new; no, that’s all from the Bible. The ranking is going to be set up in the Kingdom too. “And thine exactors righteousness”: an exactor is a tax collector. We going to be the new tax collectors on the earth; all nations going to bring us taxes. That’s what Christ was talking about in Matthew 17: then are the children free. When you’re collecting taxes, that’s when you know you’re free; as long as you’re paying taxes, you’re not free.

note.label: The Getaway 3

precepts.why: The scripture says it has double meaning. “And that he would shew thee the secrets of wisdom, that they are double to that which is!” The fire and the water in Matthew 17 are also going into sin.

note.label: The Getaway 3

precepts.why: “Prayer is good with fasting and alms and righteousness.” Notice it says righteousness: that’s the action behind the prayer and fasting. Just because you pray once or fast once the temptation is not going to jump off you; it has to be a continuation, multiple actions of belief that show you’re applying what the word says. “A little with righteousness is better than much with unrighteousness.” You brothers and sisters battling that spirit, do not sleep on it; it’s a heavy spirit. The Bible gives you ways to overcome, but you got to believe and you have to apply.

note.label: The 4 Temples In Jerusalem

precepts.why:
Christ says the same about the exactors: “Doth not your master pay tribute?” Tribute money is taxes. “Of whom do the kings of the earth take custom or tribute? of their own children, or of strangers? Peter saith unto him, Of strangers.” If you were a Roman citizen you did not pay taxes; America started that way too, then turned on its own poor.

“Jesus saith unto him, Then are the children free.” That is the part people miss: you are free when the nations pay you taxes.

note.label: LEARNING TO SEE WITH SPIRITUAL EYES | Psalm 23

precepts.why: To get there, watch the prophecy. “Why then say the scribes that Elias must first come?” Elias is Elijah. “And Jesus answered and said unto them, Elias truly shall first come, and restore all things.” See what Elijah would do: restore all things. Restore what? Restore our identity to us, restore God’s laws to us.

note.label: These Are Not Defiled With Women Part 2

precepts.why:
Some of you have been fighting pornography for years; how come you still have that spirit? Because spirits do not just leave. Christ said, “Howbeit this kind goeth not out but by prayer and fasting.” Why would Christ put that there if the spirit just left?

Some of those spirits take time, brothers and sisters. That is why it says be not hasty to credit them: there is a chance those spirits can come back.

note.label: Satan On Mt. Sinai NWO

precepts.why:
“And his disciples asked him, saying, Why then say the scribes that Elias must first come?” Matthew 17 takes place after the Transfiguration. Imagine being one of the apostles there, with Peter: they had seen Christ transfigured before them, and they thought it was about to go down, that the kingdom of Israel was about to be restored.

Our forefathers were not dummies. They knew certain prophecies had to come to pass. Remember the prophecy in the sixth chapter of 2 Esdras, which the Bishop went over on Tuesday: it says who would be ruling in the end, Esau. Esau was ruling in that time, which is why the apostles thought he was going to restore the kingdom then.

The Lord left us a trail showing us who they are today. Esau is ruling right now, just as he was then, and the son of perdition is being revealed before all of us. Who is that? Edom, Idumea. He hates his real name.

That goes back to there must be a falling away first: Israel had to be scattered, Israel had to forget their nationality, the power of the holy people had to be taken. Then Elijah comes and teaches us who we are.

Bishop taught us this years ago, and we’re not 100% but it’s up there: when the Bible talks about Elijah shall come and restore things, it might be, because Christ didn’t tell us, but the prophecy fits this man: it might have been Abba Bivens. And even though it was him, he’s back again on the earth. You think he just came and restored and that’s it? No, he’s going to keep coming; he ain’t going to stop coming until Christ returns.

Abba Bivens was the leader who started the school in 1969, and under him were seven elders. These are the elders Bishop Nathanyel learned from. Out of the seven elders, a lot of them went back into the world, but we don’t speak evil of these men, because back then they did a lot for the truth. Abba was the first street teacher, and he was killed by a bunch of Muslims while teaching in the street: they jumped him and beat him bad, and he died from his injuries. Elijah came through him, or one that came through his teachings. The spirit of life entering into us came through that line, and the Bishop came from those men and is continuing the mission he was in since his 20s, and has passed what he learned down to us.
